criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use an oblique isometric projection with upright structures and matching diagonal ground axes.
Both maintain comparable elevated, medium-distance framing across industrial plots and pylons.
different: Candidate often exposes broader, straighter parcels, while Reference crops feel slightly closer and more steeply pitched.
Candidate lower-row framing gives more area to large buildings and water corridors than Reference's open hazy terrain.

evidence.observation: Diagonal roads, upright plant, and pylon establish the elevated isometric camera.
The same isometric axes are visible, but the framing covers broader rectangular parcels.
Lower views frame broad terrain, small pylons, and distant industrial silhouettes.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use charcoal industrial metal, dark concrete, soil, and sparse amber point lighting.
Steel pylons and cyan overlays remain visually integrated with the dark ground palette.
different: Reference terrain has dense, sculpted rock and cobble relief; Candidate relies on flatter rectangular parcel and road textures.
Candidate surfaces are darker and more modular, with less weathered midtone detail than Reference.

evidence.observation: Weathered plant metal sits over densely modeled rocky and paved ground.
Industrial assets share the dark palette but sit on flatter, larger tiled parcels.
Warm soil retains strong relief, granular texture, and layered midtones.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both progress from a dark normal top row to an amber heat-like middle row and a visibly affected lower row.
Industrial buildings, pylons, and network-route vocabulary persist across the state changes.
different: Reference's lower state reads as diffuse muddy amber haze, while Candidate shows darker blue water channels and brighter cyan routes.
Candidate heat treatment is a more uniform reddish overlay; Reference retains more localized warm ground variation.

evidence.observation: Top row consistently presents the dark normal-state material treatment.
Middle row applies a coherent amber heat treatment while retaining the same kit vocabulary.
Lower row shifts to hazy muddy-amber affected terrain with pylons still recognizable.
